title: Optimization of Mouse Colon Samples for Single-Nuclei RNA Sequencing
author: Kim, Long, et al.
materials: GEM-X Flex gene expression chip kit

steps.title: Isolate mouse colon tissue
steps.instruction: Euthanize the mouse using a CO₂ chamber followed by cervical dislocation; make a vertical midline incision to expose the colon; cut the distal colon and gently pull it outward toward the cecum to isolate an intact segment; use 30–70 mg of flash‑frozen colon (validated for mice aged 3–23 months, both sexes); load a 10 mL syringe with ice‑cold PBS and flush the colon lumen repeatedly until the outflow appears clear; process the isolated colon with a gentleMACS™ Octo Dissociator equipped with coolers to obtain a single‑nuclei suspension.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize mouse with CO₂ chamber and cervical dislocation.
Make vertical midline incision and identify colon.
Cut distal colon and pull toward cecum to isolate intact colon.
Load 10 mL syringe with ice‑cold PBS; flush lumen until clear.
Use 30–70 mg flash‑frozen tissue (3–23 months, both sexes).
Dissociate with gentleMACS™ Octo Dissociator with coolers.

steps.title: Prepare FLEX single‑nuclei RNA‑seq library
steps.instruction: Prepare single‑nuclei RNA‑seq libraries according to the 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell Gene Expression FLEX reagent kit protocol (https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/flex-gene-expression/documentation/steps/library-prep/chromium-single-cell-gene-expression-flex-reagent-kits-for-multiplexed-samples); total library preparation time is 2–3 days. After library construction, assess quality on a TapeStation and expect a distinct peak around 260 bp.

substeps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s FLEX protocol (link provided).
Incubate for the required times (overall 2–3 days).
Run the final library on a TapeStation; look for a peak near 260 bp.

description: This protocol outlines the workflow for isolating mouse colon tissue, snap-freezing samples, and generating high-quality, single-nuclei suspensions for downstream library preparation. The method is optimized for 30–70 mg of flash frozen mouse colon tissue, yielding comparable nuclei recovery. This method has been validated across a wide range of mouse ages (3 to 23 months) and in both sexes, and no major differences in nuclei recovery or quality have been observed. The workflow includes procedures for mouse handling, CO2-based euthanasia, and the use of gentleMACs™ Octo Dissociator with coolers, which together support efficient and reproducible nuclei isolation.
